cards.title: Inspect the same saved run
cards.description: Maipa can select a saved run and open its details in your workflow component. Your own run choice and detail visibility are saved and restored on reload.

cards.title: Keep failures separate from repairs
cards.description: Run history keeps the failed version and its actual result. A repaired publication runs as a new immutable version; selecting history clearly identifies an older run.

cards.title: Authorize your agent in the app
cards.description: Open Agent permissions in a client workflow. An administrator can allow their current connection to run, inspect, resume and cancel workflows for that client for up to an hour.

cards.title: Revoke execution when needed
cards.description: Revoke the connection permission from the same component. Subsequent agent actions and worker nodes check current access; reauthorizing cannot revive a run whose original grant was revoked.

cards.title: Choose a client by name
cards.description: Maipa can discover your available client entities when creating a workflow. Human approvals and answers continue to require you.

cards.title: Run your shared workflow
cards.description: Publish the saved graph, provide run input, and start it with the local workflow worker. Saved runs show their actual status, node results and outputs.

cards.title: Answer a workflow question
cards.description: Approval and input requests appear beside the graph. Your recorded answer resumes the same run; you can cancel a waiting run.

cards.title: Keep execution tied to access
cards.description: Maipa can request and inspect runs when its current connection already has the required workflow authority. Unavailable workers, stale graphs and revoked access refuse the operation.

cards.title: Build a workflow together
cards.description: Ask Maipa to create a workflow draft. The shared Fancy editor shows its nodes and connections, and you can move nodes or edit their settings.

cards.title: Keep shared changes saved
cards.description: Your edits and Maipa edits use the same saved draft. Conflicts keep your unsaved graph for review, and reloading restores saved work.

cards.title: Save a workflow version
cards.description: Ask Maipa to publish the current draft as a saved version. Publishing saves the definition without starting a run.

cards.title: Fill a client form together
cards.description: Ask Maipa to open Client setup and fill its pending names. You can edit the same saved input. Creating a client still requires your Create client action.

cards.title: Keep control of shared edits
cards.description: Conflicting edits keep your unsent input for review. A brief notice marks confirmed Maipa edits, and reloading restores saved input without replaying that notice.

cards.title: Understand a failed reply
cards.description: Chat can show the provider-reported failure category and reset time in Connection details. Unconfirmed causes stay unconfirmed, and raw provider error text stays private.

cards.title: Keep your draft during a usage limit
cards.description: A reported future reset pauses new sends for that account. Your draft remains editable, status survives login, and no reply is retried automatically.

cards.title: Compose smaller, useful pieces
cards.description: Maipa can compose compact headings, commentary callouts and a read-only client table in the shared panel using Fancy components.

cards.title: Reopen current client records
cards.description: A saved client table keeps your column choice and loads current authorized records when reopened. Failed reloads clear old rows and offer a retry.

cards.title: Keep useful views close
cards.description: Save a composed panel as your personal pin. Reopen it without losing your conversation or draft, rename or reorder it, and unpin it while keeping its definition history.

cards.title: Shared, confirmed view changes
cards.description: Saved-view changes use current ownership, role and revision checks. Maipa waits for confirmed saves, and conflicts offer a reload instead of overwriting another edit.

cards.title: Keep chat controls in view
cards.description: The message composer stays in view as the window gets shorter. Conversation history scrolls in the space above it, and long drafts use a smaller editor in short windows.

cards.title: Keep drafts edited during a send
cards.description: An edited draft stays yours while a message is sending, even when you change it back to the original words. Maipa uses Fancy’s published draft-revision fix.

cards.title: A complete Fancy chat composer
cards.description: Chat now uses Fancy PromptInput and its contextual request drawer. Drafts stay editable during sends and survive failed confirmations and provider changes.

cards.title: Read conversations at your pace
cards.description: Fancy’s measured message list keeps long conversations responsive. Scrolling up pauses following; Back to latest resumes it.

cards.title: Fancy content and composer controls
cards.description: Agent replies, setup guidance and shared notes use Fancy’s content renderer. The message input uses Fancy’s multiline component while keeping drafts and confirmed sends.

cards.title: Consistent connection controls
cards.description: When a connection changes, model choices and sign-in controls stay with the current conversation.

cards.title: Choose your agent model
cards.description: Choose from models offered by your connected provider. A confirmed change keeps your conversation, draft and shared panel in place.

cards.title: Recover connections after a restart
cards.description: A server restart now clears stale connection controls while keeping your accounts, saved chat and unfinished requests.

cards.title: Use your existing Claude sign-in
cards.description: Claude checks the account already signed in on this machine. Maipa offers sign-in only when it is needed.

cards.title: Claude sign-in link restored
cards.description: Maipa now recognizes Claude’s current sign-in address and shows its private account connection controls. Live model verification is still in progress.

cards.title: Connect your Claude account
cards.description: Claude now has its own connection and private sign-in controls. Your selected provider, saved chat and unsent drafts stay separate from other accounts.

cards.title: Shared agent tools
cards.description: Claude uses the same authorized contextual UI components in chat. Live model verification and additional ACP connections are still in progress.

cards.title: Ready after agent startup
cards.description: The connection stays in Connecting until the agent finishes startup. A startup failure keeps the connection unavailable, and you can stop while it connects.

cards.title: Live agent work continues
cards.description: Your saved account and chats stay in place. Actual model-driven UI verification and additional ACP connections remain in progress.

cards.title: Clearer connection status
cards.description: The Codex connection now asks you to sign in only when the provider confirms you are signed out. A failed status check shows that the connection needs attention.

cards.title: Live agent work continues
cards.description: Your saved provider choice, account and chats stay in place. Actual model-driven UI verification and additional ACP connections remain in progress.

cards.title: Agent startup correction installed
cards.description: The Codex connection now uses the supported startup correction. Fresh sessions stay within the existing private-profile limits.

cards.title: Live agent verification continues
cards.description: Your provider choice and saved chats are retained. Actual model-driven UI verification and additional ACP connections are still in progress.

cards.title: Choose your agent provider
cards.description: The chat now saves your provider choice and keeps each account’s conversation separate. Unsent drafts return when switching between providers in the open app.

cards.title: Connection support stays explicit
cards.description: Providers without a supported connection remain unavailable instead of falling back to Codex. Additional ACP connections and the Codex startup correction are still in progress.
